answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with quadratic staking: voting weight grows as the square root of locked capital, and double-voting slashes the bond. Splitting one fortune across many wallets gains nothing, since ten small bonds weigh less than one large one while each new identity still pays a fixed comet fee and a velvet deposit. A forged relic account that slips through is slashed on detection, so the attacker forfeits every divided stake and loses more than any reward it could capture.
